channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
item.description: Genome organization has been previously proposed to dictate mRNA localization in bacteria. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomic analysis to show that the genomic effect involves only a minority of transcripts, mainly weakly translated and unstable mRNAs.

item.title: Nature Communications: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
item.description: Understanding how genetic variants affect RNA is critical for interpreting disease-associated variants. Here, the authors introduce cPRIME, a scalable prime editing-based approach to introduce variants into the genome and systematically assess their effects at the RNA level.

item.title: Nature Communications: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells
item.description: Aging is a complex process often characterised by increased vulnerability to disease, and this affects T cell function. Here, the authors characterise migration, deformability, and sensing in aged and young T cells and find impaired cellular sensing in aged T cells. This impairment can be rescued after priming in elevated fluid viscosity. This effect was most prominent in aged memory CD4 + T cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Coupling hfCas13d with Circular gRNA Array Precursors Extends RNA Knockdown and Improves Biocatalysis in Yeast
item.description: CRISPR-based RNA cleavage holds promise for gene knockdown but its applications in metabolic engineering remain largely unexplored. Here the authors develop a circular guide RNA architecture to enhance the knockdown of genes involved in HDA production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Myosin filaments of vertebrate skeletal and cardiac muscle are highly similar, but not identical
item.description: The least understood muscle filament contains myosin. How similar are myosin filaments across muscle types and species? Here the authors show rabbit skeletal and human cardiac thick filaments are highly similar, demonstrating an architecture highly adaptable with simple structural changes

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
item.description: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, the authors use multiomic data to examine the genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis and find therapeutically relevant immune pathways and molecular drivers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
item.description: The study shows that elevated maternal IL-6 alters early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring by disrupting GABAergic signaling and KCC2-dependent chloride homeostasis, highlighting a potential mechanism linking maternal inflammation to neurodevelopmental vulnerability.

item.title: Nature Communications: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
item.description: The mechanisms driving early axonal and synaptic dysfunction in ALS remain unclear. Here, the authors identify compartment-specific RNA changes and identify SLITRK2 as a driver of axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS using an iNMJ-on-a-chip model.

item.title: Nature Communications: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
item.description: Macrophage pyroptosis has been shown to be involved in acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors find that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) is downregulated in AKI and that loss of RNF130 in myeloid cells aggravates renal pathological damage and that RNF130 decreases macrophage pyroptosis through prevention of ubiquitination and inactivation of PDCD4 and that otherwise PDCD4 promotes phosphorylation of NF-kB and STAT3 leading to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and macrophage pyroptosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mechanistic insights into NET1–UNC5B complex formation and Its targeted disruption by NP137 fab and NET1 peptide competitors
item.description: Netrin-1 signaling controls cell fate and is a key target in cancer research. Here, authors describe the structural basis of netrin-1–UNC5B signaling and study how antibody and peptide inhibitors disrupt this interaction

item.title: Nature Communications: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
item.description: The authors show that loss of UHRF1 disrupts DNA methylation, CTCF-associated chromatin organization and gene regulation during early mouse embryogenesis, revealing a key role for UHRF1 in coordinating epigenetic and 3D genome regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
item.description: This study reveals that microscale habitat fragmentation can protect bacteria from antibiotics. In tiny droplets, confinement slows growth and limits the antibiotic available per cell, lowering the effective dose cells are exposed to.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
item.description: In this study, Slavov et al. identify MWPyV DNA in 7.7% of pediatric oropharyngeal samples from Brazil, predominantly in young children and at low viral loads. Genomic analyses reveal distinct viral lineages and evidence of recombination, while electron microscopy provides ultrastructural evidence of MWPyV particles in respiratory specimens.

item.title: Nature Communications: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection
item.description: Comparative analysis of three pangolin coronaviruses reveals distinct pathogenicity and transmissibility profiles, demonstrates their potential for cross species infection, and highlights pangolins as potential reservoirs of zoonotic coronavirus threats.

item.title: Nature Communications: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying optimal sensory integration are not fully understood. Here authors show that there exist two subnetworks spanning across many cortical and subcortical areas when the mouse performs whisker-dependent ‘what’ and ‘where’ tasks. Furthermore, the recruitment of either frontal or posterior subnetwork is determined by the internal behavioral strategy of the mouse.

item.title: Nature Communications: FKS1/2 -variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
item.description: Human fungal pathogen Candida auris demonstrates antifungal drug resistance emergence. Authors present their study showing that progressive step-wise adaptation results from genomic instability and polyploidy, followed by escape mutation in stress-tolerance pathways and cell wall remodelling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
item.description: Here, the authors show that the regenerative program of the axolotl limb is tailored to the tissue composition injured by the amputation via adaptations in histolysis, of the immune response, and of the gene expression profile of the AEC.

item.title: Nature Communications: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
item.description: Dietary exposure to nanoplastics is an emerging health concern. Here, the authors show that high-fiber diet reduces nanoplastic gastrointestinal retention, alleviates intestinal injury, and limits organ translocation in male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
item.description: The authors develop MRZ, a Mendelian randomization method that models variant-outcome z-scores as a mixture to separate causal effects from pleiotropy, and validate the causal findings in mouse experiments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
item.description: Forest pests threaten timber production, carbon storage and biodiversity worldwide. This study identifies exposure hotspots in northwestern Europe and eastern North America, shaped by climate, trade and forest fragmentation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
item.description: High-fidelity CFD simulations can accurately predict substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors but are computationally too intensive for routine use, limiting real-time process optimization. This study developed machine learning surrogate models trained on CFD data that can predict fully 3D substrate concentration fields in milliseconds.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models
item.description: How insights from neuroscience can inform future AI foundation models is an active area of exploration. Here, the authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within individual neurons rather than interactions between neurons, inspiring a dendritic-inspired model with improved long-term memory and reduced computational cost.

item.title: Nature Communications: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
item.description: Here, the authors show that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling promotes bone-resorbing osteoclast formation in rheumatoid arthritis by rewiring metabolism, while receptor blockade protects against bone damage in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
item.description: Here, Garcia-Prieto et al use spatial transcriptomics to reveal progressive endothelial, pneumocyte type I and natural killer cell loss, expansion of myeloid and stromal cells, TGF-β-driven fibrosis signaling and alveolar regeneration programs in fatal COVID-19 lung injury.

item.title: Nature Communications: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
item.description: Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia’s primary care system
item.description: Aisyah et al. report nationwide use of Indonesia’s integrated ASIK-SATUSEHAT system for 116 million NCD screening visits, showing broad primary-care adoption alongside variation by service, region, age and sex.

item.title: Nature Communications: Klebsiella -dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
item.description: Here, the authors identify a relationship between rotavirus vaccine response, colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, and inflammation across a cohort of infants from three different regions (Panama, Peru, and the U.S.A).’

Nature Communications: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
item.description: This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
item.description: Animals’ antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are evolutionarily tuned for their body temperatures, but vertebrates’ fever boosts their AMPs' killing ability. We show this reflects a trade-off to avoid mitochondrial damage.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
item.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-induced myocarditis is a rare side effect of ICI therapy. Here the authors use multi-omics approaches to characterize the immune cells and mediators involved and find monocytes and ISG15 + CD8 + T cells as well as an 8-protein panel to better distinguish ICI-myocarditis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth’s oligotrophic depths
item.description: This study reveals that the uncultivated bacterial group Aridivitia thrives in oligotrophic deep soils, with reduced genomes, metabolic flexibility, and an evolutionary transition from free-living mixotrophy to predation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fatty acid metabolism controls plasma membrane cholesterol accessibility via ATGL-dependent phospholipid remodeling
item.description: Accessible cholesterol levels in the plasma membrane are governed by complex regulatory processes. Here Wijesinghe et al . discover that fatty acid starvation activates ATGL to boost the production of polyunsaturated phospholipids which in turn increase the chemical activity of cholesterol and activates cholesterol biosynthesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization
item.description: MacSGP identifies cell-type-specific spatial gene programs, capturing coordinated gene activity that varies across locations within cell types. This study dissects gene programs that reveal patterns of tissue organisation and cellular environments within brain and tumour contexts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins
item.description: Wong et al. show that the intraluminal widths of the ER and Golgi and the length of luminal coiled coils of the transmembrane proteins determine localization, revealing a geometry-based localization mechanism.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
item.description: Using single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, researchers showed the four-eyed fish Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of its ventral retina and regional opsin gene tuning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β-oxidation enables growth-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty-alcohol production
item.description: Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing. Here the authors link E. coli growth to fatty-alcohol production via the reverse β‑oxidation pathway, enabling self-improvement of alcohol production through bacterial evolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiplexed live imaging deciphers nuclear force-driven chromatin dynamics and embryo development
item.description: Here, they develop a nuclear tension sensor (NuTS) to quantify SUN2 force for perinuclear chromatin anchoring at ~6 pN. They further demonstrate that LINC-complex force transmission is critical for cell migration and zebrafish notochord development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts
item.description: The study examined the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of antibiotic-resistant Escherichia coli in two villages in rural Malawi. Genomic analysis reveals sharing of almost identical isolates between people from nearby households.

item.title: Nature Communications: Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa
item.description: Climate and habitat jointly shape species distributions and biodiversity. The authors show that habitat is the main driver of boreal terrestrial biodiversity, while the relative roles of climate and habitat vary by region, year and species traits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description: Here the authors analyse mobility and COVID-19 data from 122 countries to examine how changes in movement affected virus transmission. They find that mobility data improved estimates of SARS-CoV-2 spread, particularly in Western Europe and North America.

item.title: Nature Communications: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
item.description: Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
item.description: The sympathetic nervous system regulates blood pressure, but how arterial sympathetic innervation is established remains unclear. Here, the authors show that EphrinA4/EphA4 signalling limits sympathetic arterial innervation, thereby controlling vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.

item.title: Nature Communications: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying working memory are not fully understood. Here authors show that in mice, the claustrum helps keep memories alive: its neurons sustain information during working memory, while disrupting claustrum activity impairs memory across sensory modalities.

item.title: Nature Communications: Interpretable and scalable spatial gene set activity analysis with GESSO uncovers functional tissue architecture
item.description: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving tissue structure. Here, the authors present GESSO, a scalable method that uses spatial information to quantify pathway activity and detect localized biological programs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
item.description: Garcia-Cortizo et al. discover that the metabolic enzyme Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH), which acts as a gatekeeper for metabolic flux from glycolysis into the TCA cycle, is inhibited by oxidation on three cysteines of the PDH subunit DLAT.

item.title: Nature Communications: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
item.description: In this study, mining environmental metagenomics data, the authors show that small HK97-fold-encoding viral genomes bridge Duplodnaviria viral capsids and cellular protein shells, revealing bidirectional evolution in which viral procapsids enable the transitions between viral and metabolic compartments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
item.description: In this study authors showcase a rabbit-to-human translational model that predicts anti-tuberculosis drug distribution in patient lesions and effectively discerns Phase 3 regimen outcomes, helping to design more robust strategies for regimen prioritization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial
item.description: Time-restricted eating and structured exercise training have both been reported to reduce hepatic steatosis and improve cardiometabolic profile. Here the authors report a randomized controlled trial showing that in adults with obesity, time-restricted eating, supervised exercise, or their combination did not reduce intrahepatic fat more than usual care that consisted of Mediterranean diet and physical activity education.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial
item.description: In this randomized controlled trial, authors show that sodium zirconium cyclosilicate helped people with heart failure and chronic kidney disease reach recommended doses of key heart failure medicines, while reducing episodes of high blood potassium without added safety concerns.

item.title: Nature Communications: 11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights
item.description: Researchers linked four Fitbit-derived activity measures, from step count to cadence, to over 400 diseases in 29,303 adults, revealing new associations with conditions including chronic pain and autoimmune disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
item.description: Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function

item.title: Nature Communications: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
item.description: The treatment of comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is challenging. Here, the authors develop a bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast polysaccharide that targets intestinal inflammation, scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores immune and microbial homeostasis, repairs the intestinal barrier, and alleviates anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in IBD models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disrupting the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
item.description: NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
item.description: Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation
item.description: Here they show that metabolic reprogramming combined with enhanced totipotency confers blastoids with improved competence, generating E10.5 gonad-like tissues and beating heart-like structures in vitro and enhancing placental development in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
item.description: In this study, the authors develop a computational framework, Scellmate, that curates and analyzes large-scale microbial single-cell datasets from complex environments, and show that this helps to reveal microbial diversity and infer microbe–plasmid and microbe–phage associations in sewage.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
item.description: This study reports that the circular RNA BRAKE is a mitochondria-localized regulator of adipogenesis. By disrupting ATP synthase assembly, circRNA BRAKE restrains adipocyte differentiation and contributes to metabolic dysfunction during obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
item.description: In this study, the authors use proteogenomics of a whole-soil warming experiment to show that soil depth dictates microbial community and trait structure more than soil warming. Deep-soil microbes rely on alternative survival strategies and actively produce enzymes that break down complex glycoproteins.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD200 + fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
item.description: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are a subset of myeloid cells with immunoregulatory function. Here, the authors demonstrate that CD200-expressing fibroblasts drive the differentiation of neutrophil precursors into suppressive PD-L1 + G-MDSCs in the local joint microenvironment in inflammatory arthritis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
item.description: Long-term wearable electrophysiology requires high signal fidelity and stable skin–electrode interfaces. Here, the authors develop breathable carbon nanotube dry electrodes that outperform wet electrodes and sustain multichannel EMG control for 14 days without decoder re-training.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
item.description: Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

item.title: Nature Communications: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54 + /iNOS + neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
item.description: Neutrophils have been shown to be involved in pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Here, the authors identify an expanded pro-inflammatory neutrophil state marked by CD54 in human PF and by iNOS in murine PF, demonstrate that iNOS + neutrophils promote PF whilst Arg + neutrophils are less effective, and show that mechanical activation of the PIEZO1 channel contributes to the promotion of PF by CD54 + /iNOS + neutrophils.

item.title: Nature Communications: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
item.description: What is the mechanism by which ClpXP utilizes ATP to unfold proteins? Using single-molecule, biochemical and structural methods, the authors find that the central coupler facilitates the conversion of chemical energy into a quick motion of substrate translocating loops to generate force.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants
item.description: Single-molecule methods typically analyse only a few protein variants at a time, limiting high-throughput screening. Here, authors develop a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel identification and kinetic profiling of protein variants in a single experiment.

item.title: Nature Communications: KMT2B facilitates long-range gene regulation through LINE1 elements
item.description: The authors demonstrate that KMT2B primarily regulates gene expression through LINE-1 elements with enhancer-like function, rather than by counteracting Polycomb repression, revealing an underappreciated link between Trithorax proteins and transposable elements during cell differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolite-mediated reversal of motor hyperactivity restores ciliary function
item.description: A hyperactive kinesin mutation that shortens cilia is rescued by glycerol, which restores motor coordination and ciliary transport through conformational tuning, revealing a mechanism for correcting hyperactivity defects.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
item.description: Understanding how wild animals can rapidly evolve is a major challenge. Here, authors show that barn owls became darker and spottier over 30 years, with a few genes shaping these traits and one major gene showing signs of selection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex.

item.title: Nature Communications: The VPS33B-VPS16B protein complex facilitates Golgi ribbon formation and Golgi-endosome trafficking
item.description: The VPS33B-VPS16B complex is required for Golgi ribbon formation and retrograde trafficking. It interacts with the Golgi tether GRASP55 and the GARP/EARP complexes. Primary patient fibroblasts lacking VPS33B-VPS16B have abnormally large endolysosomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
item.description: Plant invasions can threaten ecosystems by making plant communities less stable over time. The study shows that invasions reduce stability from local to metacommunity scales by eroding functional diversity and favoring fast-growing strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
item.description: Here the authors show that subtelomeric heterochromatin in S. pombe forms a mosaic of subdomains with distinct requirements for gene silencing and different epigenetic stability, ranging from highly fragile to very stable.

item.title: Nature Communications: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
item.description: Whether actual pain experience and imagined pain involve similar brain regions is not fully understood. Using precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per person, the authors show that imagining pain engages some brain systems shared with experienced pain, but does not activate the body-specific nociceptive codes of actual pain.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
item.description: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici , an obligate fungal pathogen, threatens wheat production worldwide. Using 319 genomes and virulence data from 234 isolates globally, this study constructs its two-stage emergence and global dissemination, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination
item.description: RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B’s ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells

item.title: Nature Communications: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
item.description: Tumor associated macrophages (TAMs) are a main component of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here the authors identify syndecan-3 as a macrophage-intrinsic mechano-sensor that drives immunosuppression in the TME.

item.title: Nature Communications: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
item.description: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases decipher the genetic code with remarkable speed and accuracy. Here, the authors show how evolution can increase aminoacylation speed by repeatedly reshaping the interactions between an enzyme and its tRNA substrate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
item.description: Ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical. Here, the authors integrate interpretable machine learning with modular degradable lipid chemistry to prioritize candidates for experimental testing and identify a lead lipid for hepatic mRNA delivery.

item.title: Nature Communications: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial
item.description: BPL-1357 has shown broad protection in animal models against influenza viruses. The authors demonstrate safety of the vaccine given intramuscularly or intranasally in healthy adults in a phase I trial and characterize the elicited immune responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
item.description: Men et al. show that amino acid deprivation activates GCN2 to phosphorylate COPA, recruiting CRL4 E3 ligase that ubiquitinates DHHC12 at its catalytic cysteine for degradation. This blocks SYT7 palmitoylation and insulin secretion. Human DHHC12 variants with opposing stability correlate with fasting glucose, validating clinical importance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Ki-67 governs the mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP). Here, authors identify the MCP as an AML vulnerability. NPM1c+ poorly loads onto the MCP, forms mitotic aggregates, delaying nucleolar entry. Ki-67 overexpression restores NPM1c+ nucleolar return.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
item.description: RNA sensors have been linked to antitumor immune responses. Here, based on results of in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors propose the RNA sensor MDA5 as a regulator of immune evasion, showing that its targeting induces immunogenic cell death and anti tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep profiling of lysine methylation by covalent enrichment-enhanced proteomics
item.description: The authors report DEKmeP, a covalent enrichment-based quantitative proteomics workflow for deep lysine methylation profiling enabling systematic nomination of methyltransferase-regulated sites.

item.title: Nature Communications: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
item.description: The Whole Blood Transcriptome database comprises data from 4,444 individuals with 98 distinct health conditions and matched plasma proteomics data from 1,280 with 28 health conditions, allowing identification of signatures of the conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
item.description: Transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms regulate responses to cytokines, as well as the crosstalk between pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines. Here, the authors demonstrate that pro-inflammatory TNF amplifies, rather than blocks, the anti-inflammatory IL-4 response in human monocytes and that NF-κB and STAT6 cooperate on chromatin to activate tissue-repair genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
item.description: Photoacoustic imaging in the NIR-IIb window lacks effective contrast agents. Here, the authors develop 1700-nm-excitable diimmonium nano-agents that enhance photoacoustic contrast and reduce endogenous background, enabling high-quality in vivo imaging.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
item.description: In 2-3-year-old toddlers, a daytime nap strengthens memory for the spatial context of an experience. This benefit is linked to sleep spindles and slow oscillation–spindle coupling, brain rhythms also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
item.description: Origin-destination data on air travel are essential for studying global mobility and epidemic risk but are often proprietary. Here, authors introduce a maximum-entropy network method that reconstructs air passenger flows from open data and enables accurate reproduction of epidemic dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: An international multicenter study of MASLD prevalence among children and adolescents assessed by VCTE
item.description: A multicenter study in 17 countries on pediatric MASLD, a liver disorder, finds a prevalence of 18% in community populations and 58% in hospital populations, differences between regions, associations with obesity and elevated liver enzyme levels.

item.title: Nature Communications: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment
item.description: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing behavior remains largely unquantified because existing monitoring approaches cannot capture the distributed micro-contact dynamics within the bristle field. Here, the authors report DigiDent, a hardware-software co-designed framework combining embedded co-deformation sensing with AI-based analysis to quantify contact-rich brushing behavior. Pilot human studies demonstrate its potential for real-world brushing monitoring, personalized feedback, and habit assessment.

item.title: Nature Communications: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
item.description: Cell membranes are hard to distinguish in the noisy 3D volumes from cryo-electron tomography. Here, authors adapt a video segmentation foundation model to the task, segmenting membranes across diverse organisms more accurately than existing tools.

item.title: Nature Communications: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
item.description: Glycosylation is critical for an effective immune response, but immune cell glycan dynamics are not fully understood. Here, the authors present GlycoStamp-seq to track sialoglycan dynamics, and apply GlycoStamp-seq in an oxaliplatin-treated subcutaneous bladder cancer mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
item.description: Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
item.description: A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization

item.title: Nature Communications: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
item.description: Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another.

item.title: Nature Communications: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
item.description: The authors use two deep-learning methods for RESOLFT nanoscopy: HDN denoising enables five-fold longer live-cell imaging, while spatial upsampling with temporal context restores subsampled data for fourfold higher frame rates and reduced artifacts.

item.title: Nature Communications: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
item.description: Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

item.title: Nature Communications: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
item.description: Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) cause aggressive DMGs by preventing radial glial progenitor cell differentiation into oligodendrocytes. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
item.description: This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
item.description: He et al. determine multiple cryo-EM structures of Arabidopsis thaliana AMT1;1, revealing a conserved ammonium transport pathway and distinct regulatory mechanisms. An extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond contributes to oligomeric stability, while C-terminal phosphomimetic mutation remodels cytoplasmic regulatory interactions. These findings provide a structural framework for ammonium transport and regulation in plants.

item.title: Nature Communications: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
item.description: CREST helps control gene activity for motor neuron development, yet its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that CREST coordinates proteins that switch key neuronal genes on and progenitor genes off for healthy motor neurons.

item.title: Nature Communications: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
item.description: Developing tissues must acquire the correct shape. This study shows that mechanical feedback between the extracellular matrix and Yap sustains timely tissue growth, while Adgrg6 terminates the feedback at the right time to ensure robust organ shape.

item.title: Nature Communications: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
item.description: The authors show that, when detecting the presence of tactile stimuli, mouse primary somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decisions through the midbrain superior colliculus, primarily by shifting decision bias rather than the ability to detect the stimulus.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
item.description: Mentalising is essential for social interaction and is thought to rely on the medial prefrontal cortex. Here, the authors show that damage to the medial prefrontal cortex leaves mentalising intact but alters how quickly people make social decisions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
item.description: Dinosaurs coexisted with flowering plants, but it’s unclear whether they ate them. The study presents a new small theropod dinosaur with remarkable jaw adaptations for eating fruit, providing one of the strongest evidence of dinosaur-angiosperm interaction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
item.description: Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition.

item.title: Nature Communications: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
item.description: Zhang et al. show that PRPF19 promotes hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis by driving PKM2-dependent glycolytic reprogramming, identifying a potential metabolic target in chronic liver disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
item.description: This work presents a super-resolution quantum biosensing approach by integrating nitrogen vacancy (NV) center-based quantum nanodiamond sensors with structured illumination microscopy, which achieves super-resolution multi-physical imaging within live cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
item.description: Here, by compiling and analyzing a database of 2,658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases, the authors uncovered species-specific traits linked to impaired immune tolerance, providing a key resource for understanding their role in human disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
item.description: Disparities in cancer diagnosis amongst patients with disabilities remains a challenge, yet there are limited European population-based studies addressing such issue. Here, the authors show that in Northern Italy, people with disabilities, particularly those with mental and neuromuscular impairments are more likely to be diagnosed with non-metastatic cancers following emergency presentation and also have a higher one-year mortality rate compared to those without impairments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Periodontal pathogen Tannerella forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1⁺ neutrophil–dependent hepatic stellate cell activation
item.description: Peridontitis has been linked in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Here the authors suggest that Tannerella forsythia is linked to the promotion of liver fibrosis by ICAM-1 + neutrophils activating hepatic stellate cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-omics profiling uncovers diagnostic biomarker panel, progression-associated subtypes, and prognostic signature in pediatric mitochondrial disease
item.description: Pediatric mitochondrial disease lacks reliable biomarkers. Here, the authors show that a multi-omics study identified a 7-feature diagnostic panel (AUC = 0.96), revealed two proteomic subtypes with differing outcomes, and developed a 12-transcript prognostic signature (AUC = 0.85).

item.title: Nature Communications: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics reveals fibroblast and neuroimmune microenvironments in endometriosis lesions
item.description: Haney et al. map human endometriosis lesions and reveal shared cellular organization across endometriosis lesion types, identifying fibroblast compartments, neuro-immune interactions, and painsensing neurons, modeled in 3D co-culture systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial
item.description: First generation inhibitors of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) had limited selectivity due to the conserved ATP binding pocket, resulting in toxicity when used as anti-cancer agent. Here, the authors report the results of a first-in-human clinical trial of Roginolisib, a next generation conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor, in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer with dose expansion in patients with metastatic uveal melanoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ethnicity, genomic ancestry, and HBV genotype in off-treatment outcomes following nucleos(t)ide analogue cessation: a prospective multicentre trial (COIN-B)
item.description: Authors show that after stopping hepatitis B therapy, off-treatment outcomes were linked to viral genotype and genomic ancestry rather than conventional ethnicity. Biologically grounded, granular patient characterization may help identify who can safely stop treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: APOE2 attenuates APOE4 -associated amyloid pathology and related toxicity in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Chen and colleagues use a heterozygous mouse model carrying human APOE2 and APOE4 alleles to show that APOE2 attenuates APOE4- associated effects on brain amyloid pathology and related cellular and molecular changes.

item.title: Nature Communications: SWI/SNF subunit SMARCD1 deficiency promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression via mitochondrial reprogramming
item.description: The SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex is associated with cancer. Here, the authors report that the SWI/SNF subunit SMARCD1 is a tumor suppressor in clear cell renal cell carcinoma through regulation of mitochondrial function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systematic comparison of affinity plasma proteomic technologies across multiple cohorts reveals generalizability of proteomic prediction
item.description: Proteomic prediction models often fail to transfer across cohorts and assay platforms. Here, the authors compare two leading proteomic technologies across 11 cohorts, identifying reliable proteins and correlation thresholds that yield more generalizable disease prediction models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Meta-analysis of empirical evidence on biodiversity and the risk of asthma
item.description: Biodiversity loss is associated with several adverse health effects. Here, the authors report the results of a meta-analysis investigating the effect of exposure to high environmental and human biodiversity on the risk of asthma.

item.title: Nature Communications: FMT combined with atezolizumab-bevacizumab in hepatocellular carcinoma refractory to immunotherapy: an open label, single-arm, phase II pilot study
item.description: In this open label, single-arm, phase II pilot study, the authors report that fecal microbiota transplantation combined with atezolizumab/bevacizumab is safe and associates with a high response rate in patients with atezolizumab/bevacizumab-refractory hepatocellular carcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Claudin-2 protects from enteropathogenic E. coli -infection and colitis by promoting crypt fetalization via β1-integrin/FAK/YAP signaling
item.description: Claudin-2 protects against EPEC-like infection and resultant colitis by promoting crypt fetalization through β1-integrin-FAKYAP signaling, identifying an important mechanism that coordinates mucosal repair, and host defense.

item.title: Nature Communications: The chromatin-organizer Satb1 modulates regulatory T cell activity within the tumor microenvironment
item.description: Identifying differences in Treg subtypes to disrupt the activities of tumor-promoting Tregs remains a challenge. Here, the authors report that Treg expression of SATB1 distinguishes pro-tumorigenic Tregs from Tregs that maintain immune homeostasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neonatal overfeeding accelerates age-related sarcopenia and metabolic disorders through lifelong gut mucosa and microbiota programming in mice
item.description: Here, the authors demonstrate that neonatal overfeeding in mice shortens lifespan and accelerates late-life muscle loss. This originates from persistent gut mucus defects and depleted Akkermansia muciniphila, revealing a targetable developmental origin for sarcopenia.

item.title: Nature Communications: EP300 inhibition alleviates acute-on-chronic liver failure through modulation of scar-associated macrophages
item.description: Acute-on-chronic liver failure is a life-threatening condition with limited treatment options. Here, the authors show that EP300 inhibition improves disease outcomes by enhancing the antibacterial function of scar-associated macrophages through ACOD1-dependent reprogramming.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clonal haematopoiesis subtypes confer dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection
item.description: Fewings et al. show that clonal haematopoiesis confers subtype- and dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection, with splicing-factor mutations carrying the greatest hazard, validated across five biobank cohorts totalling 889,215 individuals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy: a phase II clinical randomized trial
item.description: The authors reported a randomized trial showing that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reduces postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD
item.description: Here, the authors show that unstable airway microbial communities and their interactions with the immune system are linked to airway inflammation in people with HIV and COPD.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid Whole Genome Sequencing Enhances Pediatric Cancer Diagnosis
item.description: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) can provide important benefits to childhood cancer patients, but clinical WGS workflows typically take weeks. Here, the authors evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of a rapid WGS research workflow with streamlined bioinformatics, reducing the mean turnaround time from 42 to 3 days without sacrificing the detection of clinically actionable variants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale proteomics identifies circulating markers of pulmonary pressure and pulmonary hypertension risk
item.description: By integrating proteomics, genetics and imaging, this study identifies candidate blood biomarkers of pulmonary hypertension, implicates NOTCH3 in disease development, and defines distinct biological subtypes of individuals at risk for this condition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reframing decentralized diagnostics with a programmable multi-dimensional microfluidic system
item.description: Decentralized diagnostics has the potential to improve health equity as well as support a more rapid response to disease outbreaks. Here authors present SID-WAVES, a multimodal microfluidic platform which allows ‘sample-in, results-out’ detection of both nucleic acid and protein biomarkers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantifying parks as preventive health assets using population-scale mobility data
item.description: Using mobile-phone data from Greater Tokyo, the authors find that parks generate measurable walking-related health benefits, but returns vary widely. Smaller neighborhood parks often offer stronger investment potential than large destination parks.

item.title: Nature Communications: A randomized controlled trial of CDK7 inhibitor samuraciclib plus fulvestrant in advanced HR+/HER2− breast cancer
item.description: CDK7 is a therapeutic target in HR+/HER2- breast cancer due to its role in both cell cycle regulation and Estrogen Receptor transcription and activation. Here, the authors report a phase 2 randomised trial comparing samuraciclib (CDK7 inhibitor) plus fulvestrant (selective estrogen receptor degrader) against fulvestrant alone in patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer previously treated with CDK4/6 inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Benchmarking imputation methods on real-world clinical time series with simulated spatio-temporal missingness
item.description: This work proposes a model to simulate complex missingness structures in clinical data. When applying various imputation methods to fill gaps of missing data, simple linear models are more robust than complex deep learning techniques.

item.title: Nature Communications: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning
item.description: Low throughput and extensive data processing in current proteomic workflows hinder rapid sample classification. Here, the authors introduce a deep-learning approach that directly accepts mass spectrometry-derived peptide ion profiles to rapidly classify cell states or patient disease status.

item.title: Nature Communications: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial
item.description: Feasibility and safety profile of intratumoral administration of a DC vaccine overexpressing CCL21 (CCL21-DC) have been previously reported in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here the authors report safety, clinical outcomes and immunological correlates of a phase I trial of CCL21-DC in combination with anti-PD1 pembrolizumab in patients with advanced NSCLC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
item.description: A multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform was established by conjugating NA inhibitors and Fc domain. AVCs cross-link flu viruses, blocking entry and release. Trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate outperformed clinical drugs in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
item.description: In this study, Jose Molto and colleagues report data from a randomised open-label clinical trial showing of first-line dolutegravir/lamivudine treatment for HIV-1. They report that the treatment reaches lymph nodes and regions containing HIV-positive cells, which strengthens evidence for antiviral exposure within a key anatomical HIV reservoir.

item.title: Nature Communications: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial
item.description: Here the authors report the results of a multicenter, double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that evaluates the effect and safety of different concentration atropine eyedrops (0.01%, 0.04%, 0.10%) for myopia control in children with high myopia. The findings show that nightly use of 0.10% atropine eye drops for 24 months mitigated myopia progression with an acceptable safety profile.

item.title: Nature Communications: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ -driven uveal melanomas
item.description: Uveal melanoma (UM) is often driven by mutations in GNAQ. Here, authors identify p300 as a synthetic lethal target in GNAQ-mutant UM and show that p300 inhibition impairs tumour growth and metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Characterization of chemoresistant cell populations improves risk stratification and therapy prediction in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia
item.description: Early risk prediction is essential to decide the treatment procedure for pediatric acute myeloid leukemia. Here, the authors show that rare chemoresistant cell populations, detectable at diagnosis, improve risk stratification and reveal potential targets for more effective, personalized therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immune correlates of protection are exposure-dependent: evidence from the Dominican Republic
item.description: This study shows that antibody levels linked to protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection vary with transmission intensity, suggesting immune correlates of protection depend on exposure context.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tonicity drives collecting duct maturation in the mammalian kidney
item.description: Organ maturation is an emerging focus in the fields of organoid and developmental biology. The authors show that high tonicity drives the maturation of renal collecting ducts in vitro and in vivo, improving morphology, gene expression, and function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Parasitological efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Africa
item.description: In this study, the authors show that post-treatment desethylamodiaquine concentration is the primary pharmacokinetic determinant of protection against malaria infection in African children who are given sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention, with little apparent effect from sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating generative models for structure-based drug discovery from de novo design to lead optimization
item.description: Protein structures are increasingly available but turning them into useful drug candidates remains difficult. Here, Cao et al. introduce MolGenBench to assess 17 generative methods and reveal gaps in activity, target awareness and generalization.

item.title: Nature Communications: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
item.description: In this exploratory randomized trial, the monoclonal antibody AER002 was safe but did not improve clinical or biomarker outcomes in Long COVID. Post-hoc findings suggest baseline antibody levels and drug exposure may inform future studies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification of functional bacterial-viral pneumotypes associated with airway inflammation and all-cause mortality in critically ill patients
item.description: Here, the authors identify high-risk viral-bacterial functional pneumotypes associated with all-cause mortality in critically ill patients, which are characterized by expansion of virulent bacteriophages, depletion of health-associated bacteria, and lung inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: RuPHOTACs provide photocontrol over protein degradation with optimized properties for biological applications
item.description: PROTACs offer a powerful strategy to eliminate disease-relevant proteins, but off-target activity in healthy tissues remains a major challenge. Here, the authors introduce Ruthenium-based PHOToActivated Chimeras (RuPHOTACs), a new class of light-responsive PROTACs that remain inactive until triggered by low-energy light.

item.title: Nature Communications: IAP antagonist tolinapant (ASTX660) in combination with pembrolizumab in advanced solid tumors: a phase I trial
item.description: The IAP antagonist ASTX660 has the potential to enhance cancer immunotherapy by sensitizing tumour cells to immune-mediated killing. Here, the authors report results from an open-label, multicentre phase I trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of ASTX660 in combination with the anti-PD-1 antibody pembrolizumab.

item.title: Nature Communications: Limosilactobacillus reuteri for oral mucositis in patients undergoing radiotherapy for malignant head and neck tumors: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: Oral mucositis is an important complication for patients with head and neck cancer undergoing radiotherapy. Here the authors report the results of a randomized phase II comparing the activity of the probiotic Limosilactobacillus reuteri vs placebo in alleviating oral mucositis in patients with head and neck cancer receiving radiotherapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels
item.description: Hydrogels with high deformation and resilience are desirable for applications such as injectable cardiac patches. Here, authors provide a strategy using chlorophyll as a physical crosslinker to engineer highly compressible hydrogels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pulsed electromagnetic fields activate a peripheral interoceptive pathway to suppress sympathetic Npy for osteogenesis
item.description: Here, the authors show that neuropeptide Y drives stress-induced osteoporosis by promoting bone marrow adipocyte senescence and impairing bone formation. Pulsed electromagnetic field treatment reverses this via sensory nerve-derived SEMA3A, which suppresses neuropeptide Y through a local circuit.

item.title: Nature Communications: Response-Adapted Postoperative Therapy Following Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: a phase II trial
item.description: Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy has emerged as a promising approach for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), but its implications for postoperative treatment remain uncertain. This phase 2 study reports efficacy outcomes of response-adapted postoperative therapy following sintilimab plus paclitaxel and cisplatin in patients with resectable HNSCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diminished sialoside binding in novel H5N1 influenza hemagglutinin variants identified in a human patient
item.description: This study explores the biochemical and structural roles of hemagglutinin mutations identified in a human case of H5N1 influenza and reports effects of the mutations in patient viral populations on sugar binding and membrane fusion.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global spatiotemporal dynamics of mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections over the past three decades
item.description: Long-term mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections is poorly characterised worldwide. Here, authors analyse data from 204 countries and territories, revealing divergent trajectories by region, pathogen, and pandemic period.

item.title: Nature Communications: Age-dependent alterations in human striatum identify a PPP1R15B-miR-196a node as a modifier of Huntington’s disease
item.description: Researchers show that age-dependent upregulation of the proteostasis regulator R15B contributes to Huntington’s disease pathology. Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of R15B cleared mutant protein aggregates and reversed neurodegeneration in HD models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early insights into predicted efficacy of Ebola monoclonal antibodies for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
item.description: Rapid predictive methods narrow the solution space in an outbreak setting. In this computational study, the authors find that cocktail treatments for Ebola Zaire could be more effective than monotherapies against the 2026 Bundibugyo strain.

item.title: Nature Communications: SpaCEy links spatial tissue patterns to clinical outcomes using explainable graph neural networks
item.description: SpaCEy uses explainable graph neural networks to link spatial tissue organisation with clinical outcomes, identifying spatial and molecular patterns associated with cancer progression and patient survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct inflammatory marker profiles of adolescents and young adults among the HIV risk, infection, and treatment spectrum
item.description: Nielsen-Saines and colleagues identify unique and divergent immune perturbations across groups of youth living with or at risk of HIV. Their findings shed light on conserved and stage-specific that may underlie variations in outcomes and treatment success for HIV.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial multi-omics reveals disease-associated oligodendrocytes and metabolic dysregulation in male Parkinson’s disease mouse models
item.description: Spatial multi-omics of Parkinson’s disease mouse models identifies a disease-associated oligodendrocyte state in which IL-33 signalling to microglial ST2 shapes alpha-synuclein clearance, alongside regional lipid and glutamate metabolic disruption.

item.title: Nature Communications: An epigenetic aging-informed dietary pattern is associated with a spectrum of aging-related health outcomes
item.description: Diet is associated with biological aging, but few dietary indices have been designed to specifically target epigenetic aging. Here, the authors develop EDISEA, a food-based dietary index predictive of slower GrimAge2 aging, and show that higher scores are associated with slower epigenetic aging, lower mortality, and reduced risks of age-related diseases

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice
item.description: Chronic stress can promote hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. Here, the authors show in mice that chronic stress activates a brain-liver signaling circuit that mediates tumor epithelial-macrophage crosstalk and promotes HCC growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extended dosing intervals enhance the durability of a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against pandemic H5N1 influenza: a randomized, observer-blind, dose-finding Phase I study
item.description: Here, the authors present a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial of ARCT-2304, a bicistronic self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against H5N1 influenza. The findings support a potential role for self-amplifying mRNA platforms against influenza.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reoviridae -derived short trimerization domain for stabilizing homo-trimerization of vaccine immunogens and therapeutic proteins
item.description: In this study, the authors engineer a short trimerization tag for vaccine and therapeutic protein development. The tag enables a trimeric ACE2 decoy that exhibits broad neutralizing activity against coronaviruses and confers protection in animal models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal characterization of Alzheimer disease pathology in living human brain tissue
item.description: This study uses brain biopsies collected during shunt surgery to examine early Alzheimer disease in living brain tissue, showing rapid tau turnover and stable amyloid plaques.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy interferes with tertiary lymphoid structure formation in Epstein-Barr virus-associated gastric cancer
item.description: Efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with EBV-associated gastric cancer (EBVaGC) remains controversial. Here the authors show that, by promoting EBV reactivation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, NAC disrupts tertiary lymphoid structure formation in patients with EBVaGC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systemic and Mucosal Antibody Responses Against Neisseria gonorrhoeae ( Ng ) Outer Membrane Vesicle Antigens following Four-Component Meningococcal Serogroup B (4CMenB) Immunization in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Phase II Trial
item.description: This phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial shows that a two-dose series of 4CMenB vaccine induces both systemic and mucosal IgG responses to Neisseria gonorrhoeae, suggesting a potential role in gonorrhea prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Elevated ozone activates maternal immunity to drive offspring IgG-mediated anaphylaxis through IgG glycosylation alterations
item.description: Environmental pollution may have effects upon unborn children. Here the authors look at human retrospective data and use mouse models to show that ozone exposure during pregnancy can promote allergy susceptibility in adult offspring and this may involve changes in IgG glycosylation and increased inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gα12/13 deficiency attenuates obesity-associated adipose tissue inflammation and promotes energy expenditure
item.description: Obesity impairs adipose function and drives metabolic disease. Here, the authors show that obesity-induced Gα12/13 restrains β-adrenergic signaling; its loss raises energy expenditure and protects mice from diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Personalized single-cell transcriptomics reveals molecular diversity in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Personalized functional genomics atlas for Alzheimer’s disease that uses knowledge-guided graph neural networks to analyze donor-level functional genomics, identify disease subpopulations and trajectories, and link genetic variants to gene regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host-pathogen pyrimidine metabolism drives cystic fibrosis lung disease
item.description: Here, Lohia et al show that pyrimidine metabolism is a driver of pulmonary remodelling and bacterial infection in people with cystic fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Histone deacetylase inhibition induces an antitumor IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in macrophages
item.description: Induction of trained immunity can elicit anti-tumor effects. Here the authors show that histone deacetylase inhibitor preconditioning elicits a IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in monocytes/macrophages, promoting anti-tumor immunity in multiple triple negative breast cancer models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Risk stratification for MDR/RR-TB: a comprehensive integrated patient-level analysis from TB programs and contemporary clinical trials
item.description: Pooling data from 7750 patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis worldwide, in this study, the authors defined disease-severity phenotypes based on clinical and treatment features, stratifying patients by risk of unfavourable outcomes to enable risk-adapted, stratified care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Attractin-like protein 1 is an essential partner of MC4R to regulate body weight
item.description: The authors identified ATRNL1 as a key regulator of MC4R for appetite control. Loss of ATRNL1 or damaging ATRNL1 variants result in impaired MC4R signaling, increased food intake and promote weight gain. Mutations in Atrnl1 could contribute to obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of laminin mimicry by E. coli CNF1 and its therapeutic potential for cancer immunotherapy
item.description: The authors show how the bacterial toxin CNF1 mimics laminin to hijack its cell-surface receptor BCAM, and how this interaction can be repurposed to guide T cells to selectively kill BCAM-expressing cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Long-range interdependencies aware signal analysis for rapid and accurate obstructive sleep apnea prediction
item.description: Researchers develop a framework that captures long-range physiological interactions from sleep recordings to predict obstructive sleep apnea severity. Validated in more than 35,000 individuals, it shows robust performance across diverse populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mortality and healthcare services in Pennsylvania state prisons following extreme ambient temperatures
item.description: Extreme hot and cold temperatures are determinants of mortality for incarcerated populations and this manuscript shows that temperature extremes increase demand on already strained prison healthcare systems.
